name: Action Button
tagline: A button for canvas apps that raises OnSelect, with an optional two-step confirm.

limitations: OnSelect reaches no Power Fx here. There is no app behind this demo, so pressing the button shows what the control does and not what a maker would wire it to — which is the whole point of the control on a real screen.

The demo supplies a context.events bag with nothing bound to it, so each press raises OnSelect to nobody — the event log under the demo shows every one. The control writes its output properties first, as it does everywhere, so what a maker handling OnChange would see is here too.

Hidden is not shown: context.mode.isVisible has no switch in the demo. Disabled is — turn on Read-only in the demo's toolbar, which sets context.mode.isControlDisabled, the value a canvas screen sets from the control's DisplayMode.

presets.name: A plain button
presets.description: One press, one OnSelect. The default configuration and the one most buttons want.

presets.name: Two-step delete
presets.description: The first press asks and turns the button red; the second raises OnSelect. It reverts itself after four seconds, and Escape cancels it — press once and wait to see that.

presets.name: With a glyph
presets.description: The send arrow, which is one of the two glyphs Fluent marks as mirroring itself in a right-to-left app. Turn on Right-to-left in the demo's toolbar to see it flip.

presets.name: A long label, confirmed
presets.description: The button wraps rather than overflowing, and does not change size between its two labels — the layout a narrow canvas screen actually produces.
